page: Microsoft Azure M16bs_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance provides 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8473C processor operating at 4.0 GHz. The processor architecture includes a 105 MB L3 cache alongside specialized instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Memory capacity is configured at 128.0 GB, delivering an 8 GB per vCPU allocation. The server includes no local ephemeral storage, relying entirely on network-attached block storage options such as Azure Premium Storage, and provides no bundled GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded compute efficiency alongside steady memory bandwidth. In Geekbench testing, the platform achieves a top-tier single-core score of 2213.0, corroborated by top-quartile performance in single-threaded gzip compression at 32.93 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 13.73 GB/sec. Large-block uncached memory operations deliver 108.38 GB/sec in read throughput and 67.71 GB/sec in write throughput. In matrix and machine learning tasks leveraging architectural extensions, the server reaches 333.36 tokens/sec for small language model text generation. Multi-threaded compute metrics remain within the median range, with a PassMark CPU score of 27919.15 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 13215.0.

The 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio offers a balanced footprint for workloads constrained by memory capacity rather than parallel compute scaling. Because the instance omits bundled local storage, operational storage throughput and latency depend on remote block storage attachment. The hardware profile aligns closely with production enterprise workloads, including in-memory caching systems such as Redis, relational and transactional database management systems, enterprise resource planning, and intermediate data processing pipelines requiring substantial memory residency.
